questions.prompt: What is the main job of a vacuole?
questions.explanation: The vacuole is a storage sac for water, salts, nutrients, pigments, and some waste.
questions.misconception: Building protein is the ribosome and energy is the mitochondrion - the vacuole is about storage.

questions.prompt: How does the central vacuole help a plant cell?
options: Water pressure pushes outward and helps the plant stand firm
questions.explanation: A full vacuole presses water against the cell wall, making the cell firm - the plant stands tall. When empty, the plant wilts.
questions.misconception: Chlorophyll and energy come from chloroplasts; the vacuole's job in a plant is water storage and firmness.

questions.prompt: Why does a plant droop or wilt when it has not been watered?
options: Its vacuoles lose water, so cells lose their firmness
Its vacuoles make too much sugar
questions.explanation: Without water the central vacuoles shrink, the cells lose their internal pressure, and the plant's stem can no longer stand firm.
questions.misconception: Wilting is not about roots or temperature alone - it is the loss of vacuole water pressure at the cellular level.

questions.prompt: How do animal cells usually compare with plant cells when it comes to vacuoles?
options: Animal cells have several smaller vacuoles; plant cells often have one large central one
Animal cells have one enormous central vacuole
Animal cells have no vacuoles at all
questions.explanation: Plant cells typically keep one large central vacuole for water support, while animal cells use several smaller vacuoles for storage and transport.
questions.misconception: The arrangement differs by cell type - the giant central vacuole is a plant-cell hallmark.
